subject: Food Science
title: Lactic Acid Bacteria
description: A micro-lesson that makes Lactic Acid Bacteria usable.

hook.text: Yogurt, sauerkraut, kimchi, and sourdough all exist because lactic acid bacteria convert sugar into acid.

buildup.text: Lactobacillus and Streptococcus species produce lactic acid, dropping pH and preserving food naturally.

discovery.text: The acid creates an environment hostile to pathogens. Fermented foods are safer than the raw ingredients they started from.

twist.text: Lactic acid bacteria also produce bacteriocins—natural antimicrobial proteins that kill competing bacteria.

climax.text: Nisin, a bacteriocin from Lactococcus, is an approved food preservative used in processed cheese and canned food.

punchline.text: These bacteria preserve food, kill pathogens, and create flavor. Triple threat.

quiz.question: How do lactic acid bacteria preserve food?
options: By producing lactic acid that lowers pH and inhibits pathogens
